title: Soundness
body:
An argument is **sound** when it is valid and all of its premises are actually true. Soundness
is what makes an argument worth accepting, and [[Logical Validity]] is the part logic can
check on its own.

```
valid + true premises     = sound, and the conclusion is true
valid + false premise     = unsound, and the conclusion may be anything
invalid                   = unsound, whatever the premises are
```

Establishing soundness needs two different kinds of work. Validity is settled inside the formal
system, by a [[Truth Table]] or a derivation. The truth of the premises is settled outside
it, by whoever knows the subject matter, which is why a logic course can certify half of an
argument and no more.

The word is used a second way in [[Metatheory]], where a *system* is sound when everything it
proves is valid. Same word, different subject.
